notices.title: Automated trash and recycling pickup starts in the Pannaway neighborhood in November
notices.detail: Each household gets two 64-gallon city-issued wheeled bins, one trash and one single-stream recycling, assigned to the property with RFID tracking. Weekly curbside pickup on the usual day; only the new bins are emptied. Old bins can go to the Recycling Center, 680 Peverly Hill Road. Other neighborhoods follow in 2027. Details: portsnh.co/toter or (603) 431-2000.

police.name: Portsmouth Police Department
police.oversight: Elected three-member Police Commission (four-year terms under City Charter Amendment E); it is the department's policy-making body and meets in the City Hall council chambers.
police.logsNote: One PDF media log per day covering 5 a.m. to 5 a.m., posted about 2 to 3 days later. Each lists call number, time, call reason, street and action taken, plus a Daily Arrest Log section. The department says entries are unverified reports.

recent.title: DUI arrest after a traffic stop on the Spaulding Turnpike
recent.detail: A late-night motor vehicle stop on the northbound Spaulding Turnpike ended in an arrest on DUI and speeding-related charges, per the daily log.

recent.title: DWI arrest after a traffic stop on Arthur F. Brady Drive
recent.detail: An early-morning stop led to an arrest for driving while intoxicated and a lane control violation, per the daily arrest log.

recent.title: Arrest after a traffic stop in Market Square
recent.detail: A midday stop ended in an arrest for driving after suspension and reckless driving. A separate warrant arrest was made on Junkins Avenue the same day.

recent.title: Commission hears drone-as-first-responder proposal
recent.detail: Skydio presented a drone program that would include a public dashboard of flight logs and mission purposes. Footage access would follow department policy and state records law.

recent.title: Commission accepts about $2 million in federal grants
recent.detail: Commissioners accepted a $1,000,000 Byrne grant for the NH Internet Crimes Against Children program and $1,031,000 for IT and security, and approved $30,000 from a donor fund for rifle suppressors.

recent.title: Calls and arrests down from three-year average
recent.detail: Through Sep 30, calls for service were down 32.9% and arrests down 25.5% compared with the 2023 to 2025 average. Mold cleanup at the new dispatch center is complete and it is operating.

recent.title: Investigators renew appeal in 1982 Maplewood Avenue homicide
recent.detail: The NH Attorney General's Cold Case Unit and Portsmouth Police asked anyone who lived near Maplewood Avenue or attended the Portsmouth Beauty School in 1982 to call the tip line at 603-271-2663.

recent.title: Road closures and parking ban for Halloween Parade
recent.detail: Downtown streets on the parade route are limited to local traffic from 6 to 10 p.m. on Oct 31, and on-street parking is banned from 5 p.m., with towing.

recent.title: Coffee with a Cop
recent.detail: The department scheduled a Coffee with a Cop event for Oct 7.

recent.title: Police seek help identifying jewelry theft suspect
recent.detail: On Sep 22 a man posing as a shopper took rings and necklaces from a jewelry store on Woodbury Avenue and fled on foot. Tips go to detectives at 603-610-7534 or Seacoast Crime Stoppers.

recent.title: Commission reviews license plate reader rules
recent.detail: The department said it does not use fixed license plate readers and has no plans to buy them. Under state law, non-matching plate data must be deleted within three minutes.

recent.title: New officer sworn in, life-saving awards presented
recent.detail: A new officer joined the force, and two officers received life-saving awards for a spring 2026 emergency involving a child. The chief said staffing is limiting proactive patrols.

recent.title: 9/11 25th anniversary ceremony
recent.detail: A public ceremony at the upper City Hall parking lot honored victims and recognized first responders.

recent.title: Ambulance and fire truck replacements moved to bonding

benchmarks.note: FBI figures for 2024, the latest year with matching city, state and national numbers. Rates are offenses reported to police per 100,000 residents. Portsmouth’s small counts swing year to year (its violent crime rate ran from 113.5 to 246.4 between 2020 and 2024), and the many people who work in or visit Portsmouth aren’t counted as residents, which pushes per-resident rates up. The FBI advises against ranking places on these numbers alone.
benchmarks.homeNote: FBI, 2024. Per-resident rates; visitors and commuters aren’t counted as residents.
benchmarks.fireNote: No fire comparison yet: national fire figures don’t match how these departments count calls or staff.
